minutes.headline: Finance Committee will push a Chapter 70 inflation rider and bus-bid reform at the July 19 meeting with Rep. Scarsdale.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a discussion with a PTO vice president and lobbyist about a letter and talking points for the July 19 meeting with the state representative and DESE on funding for non-regional schools. The committee also discussed the compressed budget process, consolidating services, the budget task force charge, the town manager search and summer meeting topics. Minutes of June 13 were approved.

public_comment.topic: Two House bills on MBTA Communities and 40B were voted down by local representatives; a federal RAISE infrastructure grant program was also mentioned.
Outreach to a state senator's office about legislation letting towns assess a local income tax through home rule petitions.
Urged the select board to use unappropriated ARPA funds on small infrastructure projects, and warned about what counts as committed funds.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of June 13th as presented.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said Lunenburg is in the minimum aid category and the increase was far below inflation.
A member said the district got a small increase last year instead of nothing.
A per-student minimum aid amount was raised in the state budget debate.
A member said busing is a large and growing part of the school budget.
The speaker estimated what reimbursement at regional rates would be worth to Lunenburg.
The bus contract ends this year and will rise, with only one bidder.
A resident described unappropriated ARPA funds and small capital projects.

decisions.decision: Committee agreed to take two or three top talking points to the July 19 meeting while sending the full list in a letter.
Top priorities named: bus bidding process, a Chapter 70 inflation rider, and smart growth funding as a third.
Chair will brief school committee and select board and a draft letter is to be sent a week before the meeting, with help from Mandy Gilman.
Facilities director, town manager and finance director reports to be added to future agendas.
Chair will invite DPW, cemetery commission and the finance director to summer meetings.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee agreed to carry two or three top talking points to the July 19 meeting with the state representative and DESE, and to send the full list in a letter.
The committee named its top priorities as the bus bidding process and a Chapter 70 inflation rider, with smart growth funding as a third.
The chair will brief the school committee and select board, and a draft letter is to go out a week before the meeting.

The committee asked that facilities director, town manager and finance director reports be added to future agendas, and that DPW, the cemetery commission and the finance director be invited to summer meetings.
No votes were recorded in the minutes, and the minutes of June 13 were approved.

why_it_matters: State aid under Chapter 70 and the cost of school busing both feed the school appropriation, so the positions the committee takes to the state may shape how much of those costs falls on the town tax bill.
The bus contract was described as ending this year with only one bidder, so the bidding process is a service-cost question residents may see in a future school budget.
watch_next: The July 19 meeting with the state representative and DESE on funding for non-regional schools.
The draft letter of talking points, due a week before that meeting.
